predictions:
Pre-registered predictions, tier p2 (written to the manifest before submission; no external timestamp). P pass / F fail / ? threshold-dependent / - n.a.
Op definition: op = one Binary, Unary or Index node of a store/if expression tree, counted on the TRANSPILED circuit; casts and literal nodes count 0; each use of a sub-expression counts again (tree, not DAG); depth = longest root-to-leaf chain of such nodes.
Hypotheses (each fails iff its metric reaches a threshold; thresholds bracketed by earlier data):
  H_cone: >= 12 distinct measured registers in the cone of the `if` (10 pass, 12 fail, 11 untested).
  H_peak_live: registers (measured + register-valued stores) simultaneously live >= theta; bracket: R10x8 peak 11 pass, R12x2 peak 13 fail (register allocation pressure).
  H_alloc (hardware register allocation, the reading suggested by IBM's 6057 text): register pool = peak live registers (measured + register-valued stores) + temporaries needed by the largest stored expression (Ershov/Sethi-Ullman number of its tree: chain 2, balanced tree ~log2 leaves); fails iff pool >= theta, bracket 13 pass (R10x8) / 15 fail (R12x2); plus a separate pool of stored BIT variables: <= 257 pass, >= 512 fail (old W256/W512 jobs). Unifies the cone rule (measured registers live) and size failures only if long expressions need many temporaries; it does NOT by itself explain the old 103-op Shannon failure (small Ershov number), which this tier tests directly.
  H_pool_LR (POST HOC, fitted on the first 25 p1 probes after seeing results; only these predictions are not blind): pool = peak live registers + left-to-right expression-stack need; pass <= 13, fail >= 15, 14 unresolved (R11x2 passed at 14; alloc8/ir104/dag104 failed at 14); bit-variable pool 257/512 as above. Known exceptions: old T1 and LUT85 (pool 12, failed) and W512 (bit pool).
  H_total_reads: sum of distinct registers read over all stores in the cone >= theta; bracket 10 pass / 12 fail.
  H_cone+store_ops / +cone_ops / +unique_nodes / +depth: H_cone plus a second trigger on max ops of one store (theta in (96,103]), total ops in the cone (theta in (101,104]), unique (hash-consed) nodes (same bracket as store ops), or expression depth (known pass up to 96).
  H_historic: the old failing shapes (2026-11-06/09) still fail today; only defined for same-day replications.
Known facts: R10x8 pass, R12x8/R12x2 fail, S_12split6/chain/24split3x8 fail, S_10overlap pass (foldable), A96 single store pass, cone of 6 small stores (101 ops) pass; old failures: 103-op Shannon (1 register), 6 Shannon stores, CONE (3 registers, 173-op cone), W512 live bits, LUT85 K=8.
Latency methodology predictions (increment over a 1-bit if, Huber +/- jackknife from the round-1 estimator):
  NULL (a case identical to REF0): increment = 0 +/- ~60 ns; spread across probes = false-increment noise floor.
  placement: if REF-after (delay after the conditional X) and REFB-before agree, XORC15 increment estimated through both curves agrees within ~2 sigma for Z and X probes separately; if the X-probe excess (round 1: X median above Z in 4 of 5 jobs) is a calibration artefact it disappears with REFB.
  design (round-1 slope 28 ns/op at 16 inputs): S45_16 - S15_16 = 30 ops -> ~+850 ns if ops drive latency at fixed inputs; S15_16 - S15_4 (12 more inputs at 15 ops) -> ~0 if only ops matter, ~+100 ns if ~8 ns/input; AOC15 - AOT15 (non-reassociable chain vs tree, same op multiset) -> 0 if depth is irrelevant even without re-association, large positive if serial depth costs.
  H_ops_only: lat ~ 293 + 28.3*ops (round 1). H_ops_plus_inputs: 180 + 28.5*ops + 8*inputs. Predictions for S15_16 / S45_16 / S15_4 under H_ops_only: 720 / 1565 / 720 ns; under H_ops_plus_inputs: 735 / 1580 / 640 ns.
